walkthroughs.body_html:
Photography and Digital Media — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Photography and Digital Media brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Photography and Digital Media.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What happens when you choose a wider aperture (smaller f-number)?
options: A bigger f-number means a bigger aperture opening.
More light enters and the depth of field becomes shallower.
ISO controls the colour balance of the image.
The camera zooms in closer.

mcqs.q: Does raising the ISO simply make photos better in low light?
options: It increases sensitivity but adds noise/grain, so it is a trade-off.
Higher ISO improves image quality in all conditions.
ISO controls the colour balance of the image.
No — shutter speed has no effect on blur.

mcqs.q: Is a slow shutter speed always a mistake?
options: Yes — sharp images are the only correct photographs.
The camera zooms in closer.
No — deliberate motion blur and light trails are creative uses of slow shutters.
No — shutter speed has no effect on blur.
